A 69-year-old man with a medical history significant for peripheral vascular disease and congestive
heart failure comes to the clinic reporting lower extremity edema. He states that his legs swell during
prolonged sitting periods, but the swelling improves with leg elevation. He denies calf pain or dyspnea.
His current medications include furosemide, spironolactone, and metoprolol for managing his heart
failure. Physical examination reveals bilateral 5/5 strength and full range of motion in the lower
extremities, diminished posterior tibialis and dorsalis pedis pulses bilaterally, and negative Homan
signs. What is the most appropriate initial treatment intervention? Answer Choices: (A) Pedal pump (B)
Prescribe anticoagulation therapy (C) Perform venous Doppler ultrasound (D) Initiate compression
stockings (E) Refer for vascular surgery consultation (F) Redoming of the thoracic diaphragm (G)
Perform lymphatic pump techniques (H) Recommend weight loss and exercise therapy (I) Increase
furosemide dosage (J) Thoracic inlet release
 A. Refer for vascular surgery consultation
B. Prescribe anticoagulation therapy
C. Pedal pump

D. Perform venous Doppler ultrasound
E. Recommend weight loss and exercise therapy
F. Initiate compression stockings
G. Redoming of the thoracic diaphragm
H. Increase furosemide dosage
I. Perform lymphatic pump techniques
J. Thoracic inlet release
